articles.title: Twill Surge Foil
articles.summary: Fine grey woven twill texture, satin sheen, high metallic sparkle, subtle diagonal weave pattern. Reads as a flat grey-taupe woven film with a faint diagonal grain and a slightly dusty look; the weave itself disappears.
articles.what: Fine curved unequal warp/weft ribbons obey two-over-one twill occlusion, with underpasses, pressed crowns, parallel edge filaments and split ends. Up close: Very fine diagonal twill: tiny slanted ribbons in cream, dusty mauve and slate, with dark pin-gaps between them. Patches drift in density, so some areas look denser and darker, like worn fabric. Muted, no clean lines. From a distance: Reads as a flat grey-taupe woven film with a faint diagonal grain and a slightly dusty look; the weave itself disappears. Measured spec (average): metal 160, roughness 81, coat 112. Shine: satin. Metal: high. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: gt / sports car, open wheel, show car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Twill Surge Foil" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood and roof: wide panels show the diagonal grain
Body sides as a quiet backdrop for livery
Pale numbers vanish into the cream flecks; use dark numbers with a light outline, or a solid plate.
Large bold graphics or stripes: weave is micro, so they sit cleanly on top
Pairs well with: black, red, silver, white.
pitfalls: Not carbon fibre: no black gloss squares, colours are dusty grey and cream
Not brushed metal: it is woven slants, not straight lines
Avoid: low-contrast pale grey/white numbers; use dark contrasting numbers or outlines.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 160 (strong pearl or anodized metal), roughness 81 (satin gloss), clearcoat 112 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: low-contrast pale grey/white numbers; use dark contrasting numbers or outlines.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: large bold graphics or stripes: weave is micro, so they sit cleanly on top; solid colour blocks: let the fabric show around edges
Patterns to avoid: carbon weave or other fabric patterns: double weave turns to moire
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat: makes the weave look sealed under lacquer; fine micro-flake: adds a little glint
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Wet Apply Meniscus
articles.summary: Soft blue-grey wet film with pale streaky liquid lenses and drainage trails; satin sheen, watery and uneven. A mottled teal-grey with pale cream highlights in clouds; reads as damp, weathered sea-glass blue.
articles.what: Unequal fine elongated liquid lenses connect by capillary drainage paths; dry contact islands, pale menisci and particle wakes show liquid under film. Up close: Dense mesh of small wormy blobs, 6-15 px long, in dark slate-teal separated by fine lighter outlines and paler aqua-cream lenses between; big soft cloud zones of lighter and darker teal under the mesh. Looks like droplets or lizard-skin cells, not smooth streaks. From a distance: A mottled teal-grey with pale cream highlights in clouds; reads as damp, weathered sea-glass blue. Measured spec (average): metal 45, roughness 94, coat 100. Shine: satin. Metal: low. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: gt / sports car, open wheel, show car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Wet Apply Meniscus" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and sides: clouds read on big panels
Whole body for a damp look
White or cream numbers read; dark teal numbers vanish.
Bold stripes or panel graphics in white or navy: calm shapes over the texture
Pairs well with: chrome, white, deep navy, silver.
pitfalls: Not smooth glossy wet paint: it is a mottled cell texture
Not rain streaks: no directional trails at this scale
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, busy graphics over the streaks.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 45 (low metal, like carbon or subtle flake), roughness 94 (satin gloss), clearcoat 100 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, busy graphics over the streaks.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: bold stripes or panel graphics in white or navy: calm shapes over the texture; tonal ghost shapes at low strength
Patterns to avoid: camo, noise, crackle: doubles the mesh; fine carbon or dots: clutter
Spec overlays that work: gloss/matte patch for number plates; clearcoat sheen: more wet look
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
